# DesktopGameEngine

[Desktop](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Desktop` · class

```csharp
public sealed class DesktopGameEngine
```

Runs a game on Windows, macOS or Linux, in a window of its own.

## Nested types

| Type | Summary |
|---|---|
| [Options](DesktopGameEngine-Options.md) | How the engine starts. |

## Constructors

```csharp
public DesktopGameEngine(Options options)
```

Types: [`DesktopGameEngine.Options`](DesktopGameEngine-Options.md)

Makes an engine with these options; it does nothing until [`RunAsync`](#runasync).

## Properties

### NativeWindow

```csharp
public nint NativeWindow { get; }
```

The native OS window handle for the engine's host window, or `nint.Zero` if the window has not been created yet (or the current OS is unsupported). On Windows this is the HWND, on macOS the NSWindow*, and on Linux the X11 Window id or the Wayland wl_surface* depending on the active video driver.

### WindowMode

```csharp
public WindowMode WindowMode { get; set; }
```

Types: [`WindowMode`](WindowMode.md)

The state the window is in. Setting it asks for a change, from any thread, which starts by the next frame. Reading it says what the window is now, so it changes only once the change is complete, which can be a second later on systems that animate it. The game also sees that as a change of size. It follows the player's changes by the system's own controls too. Use [`Options.WindowMode`](DesktopGameEngine-Options.md#windowmode) to choose how the window opens.

## Events

### Initialized

```csharp
public event EventHandler? Initialized;
```

Raised once during [`RunAsync`](#runasync) after the host window has been created, but before the game is initialized.

## Methods

### ResetWindow

```csharp
public static void ResetWindow()
```

Forgets the saved window state, so the window next opens as the options say, as the `--reset-window` command-line switch does.

### RunAsync

```csharp
public Task RunAsync(Game game)
```

Types: [`Game`](../Framework/Game.md)

Opens the window and runs the game. The task completes when the game has stopped.

### Stop

```csharp
public void Stop()
```

Asks the game to stop, as closing its window does, such as for a Quit button: the frame loop ends, and [`RunAsync`](#runasync) stops the game and disposes it, then completes. Any thread may ask.
